$comment: Structured claims registry. Validated offline by scripts/check_claims.py; field meanings and the human-review process are in docs/EVIDENCE.md ('Claims registry'). 'verification' says HOW a claim was checked, using the kinds defined in scripts/check_freshness.py VERIFICATION_KINDS; a static-pattern match is never verification. skill: null means the claim backs repo tooling (e.g. a known_stale_patterns entry in schema/freshness_policy.json) rather than one skill.

claims.claim: faiss IndexFlatIP.search pads ids with -1 (scores -3.4028235e38) when k exceeds ntotal
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_rag_pipeline.py::TestFakeIndexMatchesFaiss::test_search_semantics_match and tests/examples/test_rag_pipeline.py::TestRagPipelineRealFaiss (real faiss-cpu); also observed directly: IndexFlatIP(4) holding 2 vectors, search(k=5) returned I=[[0, 1, -1, -1, -1]], D=[[1, 0, -3.4028235e+38 x3]]
claims.notes: The FAQ entry ('What does it mean when a search returns -1 ids?') states the -1 fill for IndexIVF/IndexHNSW; the IndexFlatIP case and the -3.4028235e38 (-FLT_MAX) score come from the runtime test, not the FAQ. Other faiss versions not tested.

claims.claim: sklearn.cross_validation is not importable in current scikit-learn (backs the 'sklearn-cross-validation' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestKnownStaleApisStillGone::test_sklearn_cross_validation_gone (skips when scikit-learn is not installed)
claims.notes: Only absence in the tested version is runtime-verified. The v0.18 release notes (read 2026-10-27) say the new sklearn.model_selection 'groups together the functionalities of formerly sklearn.cross_validation'. The v0.20 notes do not mention cross_validation, so the release that removed it is not verified and the pattern message does not name one.

claims.claim: sklearn.preprocessing has no Imputer and sklearn.impute.SimpleImputer exists in current scikit-learn (backs the 'sklearn-preprocessing-imputer' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestKnownStaleApisStillGone::test_sklearn_preprocessing_imputer_gone (skips when scikit-learn is not installed)
claims.notes: The v0.20 release notes (read 2026-10-27) say sklearn.impute is a 'New module, adopting preprocessing.Imputer as impute.SimpleImputer'. The release in which preprocessing.Imputer was finally removed is not verified.

claims.claim: sklearn.externals.joblib is not importable in current scikit-learn (backs the 'sklearn-externals-joblib' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestKnownStaleApisStillGone::test_sklearn_externals_joblib_gone (skips when scikit-learn is not installed)

claims.claim: openai-python 1.x no longer supports openai.Completion.create / openai.ChatCompletion.create (backs two known_stale_patterns entries)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestOpenAiModuleLevelApiRemoved::test_module_level_completion_apis_raise_removed (skips when openai is not installed; run in the example venv): both calls raise openai.lib._old_api.APIRemovedInV1 ('no longer supported in openai>=1.0.0')
claims.notes: Only openai 3.40.0 was run; the error message itself names 1.0.0 as the cut-off, which was not separately tested. The default CI test step has no openai installed, so there the test skips.

claims.claim: tf.contrib does not exist in TensorFlow 2.x (backs the 'tensorflow-contrib' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: model knowledge at authoring time; tensorflow is not installed in any environment this repo's tests run in

claims.claim: model-deployment's torch.load(..., weights_only=True) raises pickle.UnpicklingError on a __reduce__ pickle payload without running it; the same call with weights_only=False runs the payload
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_model_deployment.py::TestTorchLoadWeightsOnly::test_skill_load_refuses_code_execution and tests/examples/test_model_deployment.py::TestTorchLoadWeightsOnly::test_weights_only_false_would_run_the_payload; passed in the example-venv run of tests/examples on 2026-10-28 (327 tests, OK; ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1, Windows 11, Python 3.13.2)
claims.notes: Only torch 2.13.0+cpu was run. The release that first made weights_only=True the default, and CVE-2025-32434 (a weights_only=True bypass in <=2.5.1), come from the torch error message and NVD text read in Phase 1, not from running older releases.

claims.claim: anthropic Python SDK 2.3.0 Messages.create() raises TypeError when given temperature=

claims.notes: SDK signature behaviour only; the client points at 127.0.0.1:9 and no API request is made. Whether the Messages API itself rejects sampling parameters is not runtime-verified here.

claims.claim: evidently 0.7.23 fails to import on pandas 3.1.0: 'from evidently import Report' raises ImportError (cannot import name 'infer_dtype_from_object' from 'pandas.core.dtypes.common'), although its metadata requires only pandas>=1.3.5
claims.evidence: traceback from the GitHub Actions examples job (Linux, Python 3.13.17, 2026-10-28) as pasted by the maintainer: TestMlMonitoringBlocks.setUpClass failed importing evidently/legacy/tests/data_integrity_tests.py; requires_dist read from PyPI JSON on 2026-10-28; not reproduced locally (no pandas 3 environment)
claims.notes: Re-check when evidently ships a release after 0.7.23; then drop the pandas<3 pin and the Dependabot ignore.

claims.claim: torch.onnx.export(..., dynamo=False) traces a data-dependent Python branch into a fixed graph: for a negative input the exported model returns -2.0 under onnxruntime while the PyTorch module returns -101.0, with no error
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_model_optimization.py::TestOnnxExporterClaims::test_legacy_exporter_silently_bakes_data_dependent_branch; passed in the example-venv run of tests/examples on 2026-10-28 (327 tests, OK; ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1, Windows 11, Python 3.13.2)
claims.notes: Warnings are suppressed in the test; the exporter's own deprecation warning is not asserted.

claims.claim: mlflow.search_runs without a status filter returns FAILED runs and can rank a crashed run first by metric
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_experiment_tracking.py::TestExperimentTrackingSkill::test_best_run_ignores_failed_runs; passed in the example-venv run of tests/examples on 2026-10-28 (327 tests, OK; ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1, Windows 11, Python 3.13.2)
claims.notes: Run against mlflow 3.16.1 (the local example venv). requirements-examples.txt now pins 3.17.2 because of three published advisories; test_experiment_tracking also passed 7/7 against mlflow 3.17.2 in a separate venv on 2026-10-28. The class is opt-in: it skips unless ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1 or ML_AI_SKILLS_REQUIRE_EXAMPLE_DEPS=1.

claims.claim: mlflow.sklearn.log_model/save_model default to serialization_format=None, which resolves to skops outside Databricks, while mlflow.sklearn.autolog defaults to cloudpickle
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_experiment_tracking.py::TestExperimentTrackingSkill::test_serialization_defaults_match_the_gotcha; passed against mlflow 3.17.2 in a separate venv on 2026-10-28 (ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1, Windows 11, Python 3.13.2); the Databricks branch was read from mlflow/sklearn/__init__.py (_get_default_serialization_format), not executed
claims.notes: On mlflow 3.16.1 the signature default was the literal 'skops'; CI on 3.17.2 failed the earlier wording. The class is opt-in: it skips unless ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1 or ML_AI_SKILLS_REQUIRE_EXAMPLE_DEPS=1.

claims.claim: The stdlib JSON-Schema subset validator (skills_lib.schema_errors) gives the same errors as jsonschema's Draft202012Validator with FormatChecker on every repo skill's frontmatter and on the mutated-frontmatter set, apart from the one documented trailing-newline pattern deviation
claims.evidence: tests/test_schema.py::TestAgreementWithJsonschema; passed in the stdlib unit-suite run on 2026-10-28 (scripts/quality_report.py --collect-tests --suite unit, global Python 3.13.2 on Windows with PyYAML 6.0.3 and jsonschema 4.26.0 installed)
claims.notes: The class skips when jsonschema is not installed (as in the stdlib-only CI unit job); CI's unit-with-dev-deps job fails if it skips.

claims.claim: Inside the supported subset, skills_lib's frontmatter parser returns the same values as yaml.safe_load for every repo SKILL.md and eval case file and for seeded random documents
claims.evidence: tests/test_skills_lib.py::TestYamlCompatibility; passed in the stdlib unit-suite run on 2026-10-28 (scripts/quality_report.py --collect-tests --suite unit, global Python 3.13.2 on Windows with PyYAML 6.0.3 and jsonschema 4.26.0 installed)
